name: Getaway
description: Getaway is a Punjabi-origin shedding game in which players race to empty their hands while avoiding pickup penalties triggered by off-suit breaks (tochoo or thulla).

overview.description: Getaway is a Punjabi-origin shedding game in which players race to empty their hands while avoiding pickup penalties triggered by off-suit breaks (tochoo or thulla).

history.origins: Documented as a Punjabi family and social game under names including Getaway and Bhabhi, with related forms in Bangladesh and South India.
timeline: 20th century: Established as a regional shedding game in Punjab households.
2000s onward: Spread through online descriptions and diaspora play groups.
2020s: Rule descriptions and variant notes expanded to include regional forms such as Donkey.
history.cultural: Modern rulesets increasingly prefer neutral naming while preserving traditional gameplay.
history.evolution: Core mechanism remained stable: follow suit when possible, and interrupted tricks force card pickup by highest led-suit player.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack with rank order A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards as evenly as possible clockwise; some players may have one extra card.

rules.objective: Get away by shedding all cards; last player still holding cards loses.
rules.gameplay: Opening trick: Ace of Spades holder leads, everyone contributes one card, and this first trick is always discarded. From second trick onward, leader is highest card of previously led suit. Players must follow led suit if they can. If a player cannot follow and plays another suit (tochoo), trick ends immediately and later players do not play to that trick. Highest card of the led suit picks up all cards played to that interrupted trick and leads next. If everyone follows suit, trick goes to waste and highest led-suit player leads next. Players who empty hand are out, except a player with lead power may need to draw from waste and continue under common rule.
keyRules: First trick is a mandatory full trick and always discarded.
From trick two onward, first valid off-suit break immediately stops trick.
Interrupted trick pickup goes to the highest card of led suit, not to the breaker.
Some tables allow taking all cards from immediate-left active player before a trick.

strategy.basic: Avoid becoming temporary high card on suits where later players are likely void.
strategy.intermediate: Manage lead control so that dangerous suits are led when opponents behind you are still likely to follow.
strategy.advanced: Use pickup and optional take-from-left timing to rebalance suit distribution and avoid forced endgame draws.
tips: Winning tricks is useful only when it helps you shed safely.
Track which players are likely void in each suit to predict interruption risk.

variations.name: Take from Left
variations.description: Before a trick, a player may take all cards from immediate-left active player in many local rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes only who may take cards and when; no engine constant overrides documented yet.

variations.name: Counterclockwise Direction
variations.description: Some tables play and deal in anticlockwise direction with mirrored take-card rule.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Direction and take-from-neighbour side are procedural; no engine overrides mapped for this variant.

variations.name: Donkey
variations.description: Related Kerala variant introduces trump suit when first off-suit is played.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Donkey adds trump and different trick resolution; full engine overrides would require separate Donkey spec.

scoring.description: No formal point count is required; hand loser is the final player still holding cards.
scoring.winCondition: Avoid being the last remaining player with cards.

synthesis.shortDescription: Avoidance shedding game where off-suit breaks can dump trick cards back onto the current high player.

hero.subtitle: Punjabi Shedding Game
hero.tagline: Shed fast and avoid the pickup trap.
